profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary: I am a very dedicated individual to my interests and hobbies, which is why I decided to make my hobbies into my work. I have a long history with games and computers. I took this passion and furthered myself through college at PSU - Behrend. During my time there I also developed my skills in translation and localization through volunteering at NanoDesu Translations. For this online organization I coordinate a small team with myself as the project translator, community manager, and contact the author of the novel for any official business.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Operated in microservice, plugin, and standalone service architectures to provide
support and enhancements for existing functionality. Analyzed and executed
programmatic performance benefits resulting in an estimated 15% increase in speed. 
Modified the existing local library structure into a microservice. Created a dynamic
code generator to keep the plugin APIs up to date. Led design and development on a
standalone tool incorporated into our primary algorithm.
positions.insights: Skills: Spring Boot · Application Programming Interfaces (API)

positions.title: Translator
positions.description:
Volunteer Japanese to English translator in the NanoDesu Translations group. My current project is the webnovel: Vermillion – Étranger à L'arc Rouge.
Responsibilities include:
- Weekly Reports
- Team Leader
- Community Management
- Handle Translations
- Review Edited Material
- Assist Other Translators

volunteerExperiences.companyName: Third Street Alliance for Women and Children
volunteerExperiences.description: A nearby church sponsors a Christmas dinner for the homeless and impoverished in Easton, PA. My role was in assisting cleaning and preparing the gymnasium for the guests, as well as minor assistance in food preparation.

company.name: Third Street Alliance for Women and Children

volunteerExperiences.companyName: Third Street Alliance for Women & Children
volunteerExperiences.description: After receiving the proper rank to instruct others in Taekwondo, I was responsible for running one to two classes a week. Class size ranged from five to thirty students with ages varying from five to adults. The classes were often run with supervision, but were occasionally run without.
